title: Target Circuit Matching in Large-Scale Netlists Using GNN-Based Region Prediction
problem: Subgraph matching in circuit verification struggles with large-scale circuits; traditional rule-based methods lack generalization, and node-to-node approaches are computationally inefficient.
motivation: Efficient subgraph matching enables faster circuit verification and design exploration for large chips.
method: Proposes GNN-based approach predicting regions of high probability for containing target circuits. Constructs negative samples for accurate target circuit detection, develops method to directly extract subgraph embeddings capturing global information, avoiding inefficient per-candidate GNN application.
key_novelty: GNN-based region prediction for efficient subgraph matching reducing per-candidate computation.
contributions: GNN-based target region prediction eliminating per-candidate subgraph matching
Negative sample construction for accurate circuit detection
Direct subgraph embedding extraction capturing global circuit information
Significantly outperforms existing methods in time efficiency and prediction accuracy

metrics.method: time efficiency and region prediction accuracy

limitations: Evaluation details sparse in abstract; specific benchmark sets and comparison metrics not fully specified.
primary_theme: GNN-based efficient subgraph matching for circuit verification
